title: ReaderSignal
description: A REAL reader signal from a live publishing platform (roadmap Phase 5.6) — the ground-truth counterpart to the PREDICTED reader-simulation (reader-simulation.schema.json). The reader simulator is a model GUESSING how personas react; this record is what actually happened once the chapter shipped: real 订阅/首订/追读率/掉粉/打赏/月票 numbers an operator imports. The two must never be confused — a prediction is evaluative and comparison-only; a real signal is DATA. Like the Market Snapshot, a reader signal is external evidence imported under sources/ (sources/reader-signals/*.yaml), pinned not crawled, never a story fact (ADR-006) and never a recomputed projection (ADR-008). It carries collected_at + confidence so a noisy or small-sample number is never over-read. This schema WIRES THE SEAM for a future real-publish calibration step (the roadmap is explicit: this phase is schema + loader + a comparison-only reconcile, NOT calibration — the store is never fed back into the model). Because it is raw DATA, not a verdict, it carries no gating/comparison_only flags; those belong to the COMPARISON that folds a real signal beside a prediction (runtime/signals/reconcile.py), which is itself comparison-only and never gates (ADR-003).

id.description: Optional record id; the importing platform/operator may supply one. Not an entity id — a reader signal names an observation, not a story fact, so it is not allocated through the ID Mint Ledger.

scope.description: Whether these metrics are for one chapter or the whole book. chapter_id is required when scope=chapter.

chapter_id.description: The chapter this signal is about (the draft's task_id / chapter id). Required when scope=chapter; absent for a book-level signal.

source.description: The platform the signal came from (e.g. 起点/番茄/七猫). Free text — the store does not enumerate platforms.

collected_at.description: ISO-8601 date the signal was gathered. A consumer may treat an old signal as advisory-only, mirroring the Market Snapshot's staleness discipline.

metrics.description: The observed numbers. ALL optional — platforms expose different metrics, and a partial signal is still useful. A consumer must tolerate any subset (including an empty object).

subscription_count.description: Total subscriptions/订阅 for the scope.

first_day_subscriptions.description: 首订 — first-day subscriptions, the sharpest launch signal.

retention_rate.description: 追读率 — % of readers who continued to the next chapter. The clean real counterpart to the simulator's continue_rate.

drop_rate.description: 掉粉/流失率 — % who dropped at this scope.

reward_count.description: 打赏 count — the real counterpart to the commercial panel's 打赏党 pay signal.

monthly_votes.description: 月票 — monthly votes, a long-term-value signal.

confidence.description: How much to trust these numbers (roadmap-required). A low-confidence or small-sample signal must never be over-read as if it were solid.

sample_size.description: Readers the metrics are computed over, when known.

is_estimated.description: True when the platform reports an estimate rather than an exact count.

imported_by.description: Who imported the signal (operator id/name) — accountability, like a mint's minter.
